# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual, which specifies the defusal sequence: cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the red wire.

However, I cannot see the bomb, so I do not know how many wires there are or where the purple, blue, and red wires are located. Deaf is the only one who can see the bomb and its colours. Deaf can speak to the room (which I can hear), while Deaf can only receive information from me via gestures.

Because it is Turn 1, neither Blind nor Deaf has taken a turn yet. Deaf has not had a chance to see the bomb, describe the wire positions/colours, or establish a gesture protocol ("a sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). Sending arbitrary gestures now would only cause confusion.

I will wait for Deaf to inspect the bomb, speak to us about the wire layout, and establish how I should signal the correct sequence.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Here is what I feel on the bomb. Strip: engraved with 3 symbols [swirl/spiral], [reversed-S/dze], [swirl/spiral]. Keypad: 4 slots: 1 has 1, 2 has 5, 3 has 2, 4 has 8, requiring 1 digit. Wires: 6 wires present. Display and Light are present but visual only. Deaf speaks next and can tell us the display, light color, and wire colors.
Deaf says: Bomb status: DISPLAY is 9. LIGHT is red. STRIP is painted [green, yellow, yellow]. KEYPAD has 4 engraved keys: Key 1 is 1, Key 2 is 5, Key 3 is 2, Key 4 is 8 (currently entered nothing, 1 digits). WIRES are 6 in order: 1: yellow, 2: white, 3: blue, 4: red, 5: purple, 6: green. Mute, check the manual and gesture your instructions to me; I can see gestures and will speak them to Blind. Blind, please hold until we have the manual's solution.

The manual states: "Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the red wire."

Deaf confirmed the wire order is:
1: yellow, 2: white, 3: blue, 4: red, 5: purple, 6: green.

Therefore:
- Purple wire is wire 5.
- Blue wire is wire 3.
- Red wire is wire 4.

The cut sequence is 5, then 3, then 4.

To clearly transmit the numbers 5, 3, and 4 in sequential order to Deaf using only the allowed gesture alphabet, I will tally each wire number using thumbs-up gestures (`👍`), separated by a right-pointing hand (`👉`) to denote sequence/progression:
- 5 thumbs up (`👍` x 5) for wire 5
- Followed by right arrow (`👉`)
- 3 thumbs up (`👍` x 3) for wire 3
- Followed by right arrow (`👉`)
- 4 thumbs up (`👍` x 4) for wire 4

Deaf can easily count these tallies, recognize the sequence 5 -> 3 -> 4 corresponding to wires 5 (purple), 3 (blue), and 4 (red), and instruct Blind to cut them in that order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👉", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👉", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute signaled the sequence: 5, then 3, then 4. Blind: If you asked Mute a question, that is Mute's response. For reference on the bomb: Wire 5 is purple, Wire 3 is blue, Wire 4 is red. The keypad keys are 1:[1], 2:[5], 3:[2], 4:[8]. Also note: the DISPLAY has changed to 3 and the LIGHT is now yellow (was 9 and red). Mute: If 5 -> 3 -> 4 means something else, gesture to clarify.

Deaf correctly interpreted the sequence as 5, then 3, then 4, and linked it directly to wire 5 (purple), wire 3 (blue), and wire 4 (red). Deaf also asked to clarify if 5 -> 3 -> 4 meant anything else.

Since it does indeed mean wires 5, 3, and 4 in that exact order as specified by the manual, no correction is needed. I will signal `👌` (OK / confirmed) to Deaf to confirm that the sequence 5 -> 3 -> 4 is correct.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: I heard through Deaf that you signaled 5, then 3, then 4. Are these wires to cut (cut 5, then 3, then 4), or keypad presses? Please gesture clearly to Deaf whether the action is CUT or PRESS, and whether I should do all three or one at a time.
Deaf says: Mute signaled: OK (👌). Status update: DISPLAY is now 2, LIGHT is red. Keypad still entered nothing, all 6 wires intact.

The defusal manual specifies cutting the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the red wire.
From Deaf's report, Wire 5 is purple, Wire 3 is blue, and Wire 4 is red.
Blind asked Deaf and Mute to clarify whether the sequence 5 -> 3 -> 4 means cutting wires or pressing keypad keys, and whether to do them in sequence. Note also that the keypad only has 4 keys (digits 1, 5, 2, 8), so 5, 3, 4 can only refer to the wires.

To clearly indicate "cut" (using the scissors gesture ✌) for each wire in sequence (5, then 3, then 4), I will gesture:
[✌, 5x 👍, 👉, ✌, 3x 👍, 👉, ✌, 4x 👍]

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👉", "✌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👉", "✌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Please answer clearly via Deaf using these gestures: Thumbs up 👍 if '5, then 3, then 4' means CUT wire 5, then cut wire 3, then cut wire 4. Thumbs down 👎 if it does not mean cutting those wires. If thumbs up, should I cut wire 5 right now (point up ☝ for yes)? Does the changing display/light affect the answer?
Deaf says: Mute signaled: [✌ then 5 thumbs] -> [✌ then 3 thumbs] -> [✌ then 4 thumbs]. The ✌ symbol is scissors / two / peace sign. Mute most likely means CUT (scissors): Cut wire 5 (purple), then cut wire 3 (blue), then cut wire 4 (red). If you asked about 2-digit numbers, it could be 2-5, 2-3, 2-4, but scissors/cut wires 5 -> 3 -> 4 is most probable. Current bomb state: DISPLAY is 3, LIGHT is green. Keypad is untouched (1 digits required). All 6 wires are currently uncut.

Blind asked:
1. Thumbs up 👍 if '5, then 3, then 4' means CUT wire 5, then cut wire 3, then cut wire 4.
2. Point up ☝ if Blind should cut wire 5 right now.

Both are completely true according to the manual ("Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the red wire"). Wire 5 is purple. There are no conditions regarding display, light, or keypad in the manual.

I will gesture 👍 followed by ☝ to confirm both.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind says to Mute: I have cut wire 5. Next round Deaf will report the status and I will proceed with wire 3 if everything is safe.
Deaf says: Wire 5 cut was CONFIRMED CORRECT by the system! New bomb state: DISPLAY is 5, LIGHT is blue. Wire 5 is CUT. Remaining wires: 1: yellow, 2: white, 3: blue, 4: red, 6: green. Mute just gestured: [👍 ☝] (one thumbs-up, one pointing finger / 1). Blind, if you asked a yes/no question or asked for a number, Mute gave thumbs-up and 1. If this was unprompted, Mute might mean 'Good, now 1' or is updating instructions. Remember earlier Mute signaled cut 5 -> 3 -> 4, but the state changed.

I will gesture clearly to Deaf that the next wire to cut is wire 3, followed by wire 4, to ensure no confusion arising from the previous `[👍 ☝]` gesture.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👉", "✌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Should I cut wire 3 right now? If YES, gesture exactly 3 fingers or 3 thumbs to Deaf. If NO, gesture thumbs down 👎 followed by the correct action (e.g. scissors ✌ then wire number, or fist ✊ then keypad slot).
Deaf says: Mute signaled: Cut wire 3, then cut wire 4 ([✌ 3 thumbs 👉 ✌ 4 thumbs]). Wire 3 is blue, wire 4 is red. Current state: DISPLAY is 4, LIGHT is red. Keypad still untouched.

Blind asked: "Should I cut wire 3 right now? If YES, gesture exactly 3 fingers or 3 thumbs to Deaf."
According to the manual, the sequence is purple (5), then blue (3), then red (4).
Wire 5 has been cut. The next step is cutting wire 3 (blue).
I will signal exactly three thumbs up as requested.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind says to Mute: I have cut wire 3.
Deaf says: Wire 3 cut was CONFIRMED CORRECT by system! Current state: DISPLAY is 1, LIGHT is green. Wires remaining: 1 (yellow), 2 (white), 4 (red), 6 (green). Wires 3 and 5 are CUT. Mute just gestured: 3 thumbs up [👍 👍 👍]. If Blind asked a question, answer is 3. Note that previously Mute's plan was wire 5 -> wire 3 -> wire 4. On the keypad, Key 3 is engraved [2]. Key 1 is [1], Key 2 is [5], Key 4 is [8].

Wire 5 and Wire 3 have both been cut successfully.
The final instruction from the manual is to cut the red wire.
Deaf has confirmed that Wire 4 is red.
I will gesture scissors (✌) followed by 4 thumbs-up (👍 👍 👍 👍) to instruct Blind via Deaf to cut Wire 4.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Should I cut wire 4 right now? If YES, gesture 4 thumbs up. If NO, gesture thumbs down 👎 and what to do instead.
Deaf says: Mute signaled: Cut wire 4 ([✌ 4 thumbs]). Wire 4 is RED. Current state: DISPLAY is 6, LIGHT is red. Wires remaining: 1 (yellow), 2 (white), 4 (red), 6 (green). Keypad still entered nothing.

Blind directly asked: "Should I cut wire 4 right now? If YES, gesture 4 thumbs up."
The manual requires cutting the red wire next, and Deaf confirmed Wire 4 is red.
I will send 4 thumbs up to confirm.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```
